title: The Vedas and Upanishads

explain.say: The Vedas are the oldest sacred texts of Hinduism, hymns and teachings in an early form of Sanskrit. Hindus call them shruti, what was heard: tradition says ancient sages heard them in deep meditation rather than making them up.

draw.text: Shruti: what was heard by the sages, or rishis

explain.say: There are four Vedas. The Rigveda, the oldest, is a collection of hymns of praise; the Samaveda sets verses to melodies; the Yajurveda gives words for rituals; and the Atharvaveda has prayers for healing and everyday life.

items: Samaveda | Verses set to melodies for chanting
Atharvaveda | Prayers for healing and daily life

draw.text: The Gayatri mantra comes from the Rigveda

explain.say: For many centuries the Vedas were passed on by memory, from teacher to student, with chanting methods so exact that the words have been kept with remarkable care. Vedic chanting is honoured by UNESCO as world heritage.

Each Veda has layers: hymns, ritual guides, forest texts and, last, the Upanishads. The Upanishads are thoughtful dialogues between teachers and students about the deepest questions: who am I, and what is real?

draw.text: The Upanishads are also called Vedanta, the end of the Vedas

explain.say: The Upanishads teach about Atman, the true self within you, and Brahman, the ultimate reality behind everything. Their boldest idea is that these are one, as in the famous words tat tvam asi, you are that.

draw.text: Tat tvam asi: you are that
Atman = Brahman: the self and ultimate reality are one

items: About 1000 to 500 BCE: other Vedas, Brahmanas

faq.a: The Vedas are the oldest sacred texts of Hinduism: collections of hymns, prayers, ritual words and philosophy in early Sanskrit. The word Veda means knowledge, and Hindus regard them as shruti, revealed truth heard by ancient sages.
The four Vedas are the Rigveda, hymns of praise; the Samaveda, melodies for chanting; the Yajurveda, words for rituals; and the Atharvaveda, prayers for healing and everyday life.
asks: What is the difference between the Vedas?

faq.a: The Rigveda is the oldest. It has 1,028 hymns arranged in ten books called mandalas, many addressed to deities such as Agni, fire, and Indra. Many scholars date it to roughly 1500 to 1000 BCE.
asks: How many hymns are in the Rigveda?

faq.a: Hindu tradition holds that the Vedas were not written by any person but were heard by ancient sages, the rishis, in deep meditation, and then passed on. Many hymns carry the names of the rishi families who handed them down.
asks: Who is the author of the Vedas?

faq.a: Many scholars date the Rigveda to about 1500 to 1000 BCE, making it one of the oldest religious texts still in use. Hindu tradition sees the Vedas as eternal, without a beginning in time.
asks: Are the Vedas the oldest books?

faq.q: How were the Vedas kept for so long without writing?
faq.a: They were memorised and chanted, teacher to student, using methods such as reciting the words in different patterns to catch mistakes. This oral tradition kept them carefully for many centuries before they were written down, and UNESCO honours Vedic chanting as cultural heritage.
asks: Were the Vedas passed down orally?
How did people remember the Vedas?
When were the Vedas written down?

faq.a: The Upanishads are philosophical texts that form the last part of the Vedas, so they are called Vedanta, the end of the Vedas. They are often dialogues between a teacher and a student about the self, reality and liberation.
Over 200 texts are called Upanishads, but about 13 are counted as the principal ones, such as the Brihadaranyaka, Chandogya, Katha and Isha. A traditional list names 108.
asks: How many principal Upanishads are there?

faq.a: Atman is the true self, the deepest part of you beyond body and mind. Brahman is the ultimate reality behind the whole universe. The Upanishads teach that, at the deepest level, Atman and Brahman are one.
asks: What do the Upanishads say about the self?

faq.q: What does tat tvam asi mean?
faq.a: Tat tvam asi means you are that. In the Chandogya Upanishad, the sage Uddalaka teaches his son Shvetaketu that the hidden essence of everything is also his own true self.
asks: What does you are that mean in the Upanishads?

faq.a: The Gayatri mantra is a verse from the Rigveda, a prayer to the divine light of the sun, Savitr, asking it to inspire our minds. It is one of the most widely chanted Vedic verses.
asks: Where does the Gayatri mantra come from?
Is the Gayatri mantra from the Vedas?
What is the most famous Vedic verse?

faq.q: Are the Upanishads part of the Vedas?
faq.a: The Upanishads are part of the Vedas, their final layer. The earlier parts are mostly hymns and guides for rituals, while the Upanishads turn inward to ask about the self and ultimate reality.
asks: How are the Upanishads different from the Vedas?
Do the Upanishads come after the Vedas?

faq.a: Shruti, what was heard, means texts regarded as revealed, such as the Vedas and Upanishads. Smriti, what is remembered, means later texts passed down by tradition, such as the epics, the Puranas and law books.
asks: Is the Gita shruti or smriti?

faq.q: Who translated the Upanishads into other languages?
faq.a: In 1657 the Mughal prince Dara Shikoh had about 50 Upanishads translated into Persian. A Latin version made from it reached Europe, where thinkers like Schopenhauer admired them.
asks: When did the Upanishads reach Europe?
Were the Upanishads translated into Persian?

facts: There are four Vedas: the Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda.
The Rigveda, the oldest Veda, has 1,028 hymns in ten books called mandalas.
Over 200 Upanishads are known, and about 13 are counted as principal.
Many scholars date the Rigveda to roughly 1500 to 1000 BCE and the oldest Upanishads to about 700 to 500 BCE.
The phrase tat tvam asi, you are that, comes from the Chandogya Upanishad.
A famous prayer of the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad asks: lead me from the unreal to the real, from darkness to light, from death to immortality.

quiz.say: Which is the oldest of the four Vedas?
quiz.why: The Rigveda, with its 1,028 hymns, is the oldest of the four Vedas.

wrong.1: The Samaveda draws many of its verses from the Rigveda, so it came later.
wrong.2: The Atharvaveda is generally thought to be the latest of the four.
wrong.3: The Gita is not one of the Vedas; it is part of the Mahabharata.

quiz.say: A student asks, what is the true self inside me? Which part of the Vedas explores that question most?
quiz.show: Which part of the Vedas explores the true self?
quiz.why: The Upanishads are the philosophical part of the Vedas and teach about Atman, the true self, and Brahman.

wrong.1: The Brahmanas explain how to perform rituals, not mainly the nature of the self.
wrong.2: The Samaveda sets verses to music for chanting.

quiz.say: The Vedas were kept by memory for centuries before being written down. What does this tell us about the people who kept them?
quiz.show: What does centuries of oral memory tell us?

options.show: They valued exact chanting very highly
options.say: They valued exact, careful chanting very highly

options.show: They did not care about the words
options.say: They did not care about the words

options.show: Paper had not been invented anywhere
options.say: Paper had not been invented anywhere

quiz.why: Elaborate memory methods were developed to keep every sound exact, which shows deep care for the sacred words.

wrong.1: The opposite is true; they took great care over every word and sound.
wrong.2: Oral teaching was a choice of method and reverence, not simply a lack of writing material.
